title: 1,200 Volunteers Tried to Reproduce 2,200 AI Papers
summary: Hugging Face ran a three-week community hackathon in which more than 1,200 people took papers from ICML, one of the field's biggest machine learning conferences, and tried to re-run the work themselves.

title: Google Releases Gemini 3.7 Flash
summary: Google published Gemini 3.

title: Someone Followed 657,607 Links to See How Much of the Web Is Gone
summary: A researcher traced 657,607 links to find out how many still lead anywhere.

title: The US Government Ran a Mass Surveillance Campaign Against Protesters
summary: The Guardian reports that US authorities carried out broad digital spying on left-wing and anti-ICE protesters.

title: Mistral Updates Its Document-Reading Model
summary: Mistral shipped OCR 4.

title: One Log Line, 110 Kilobytes of Disk Writes
summary: A bug report against systemd — the software that starts and supervises services on most Linux servers — shows that writing a single line to the system log can trigger 49 KB or more of actual disk writes on the ext4 filesystem, and 110 KB or more on btrfs.

title: Breaking a Giant AI-Written Pull Request Into Reviewable Pieces
summary: GitHub published a method for stopping coding agents from dumping one enormous change into review.

title: Google Is Making AI That Works on Data It Cannot Read
summary: Google published how it is using homomorphic encryption — a method that lets a computer run calculations on encrypted data without ever unlocking it — to make private AI features practical in real products rather than just in research papers.

title: Where Open AI Models Actually Stand This Summer
summary: Hugging Face published its half-yearly review of open models — the ones anyone can download and run on their own machines.

title: Firefox Is Now the Last Major Browser Where uBlock Origin Still Works
summary: Chrome and the other Chromium-based browsers have finished phasing out the extension format uBlock Origin depends on, leaving Firefox as the only major browser where the ad blocker still runs in full.

title: A New Open Coding Model Arrives With Security Skills Attached
summary: Z.

title: What 50 Open Source Projects Learned About Security in the AI Era
summary: GitHub wrote up the fourth round of its Secure Open Source Fund, where 50 projects combined AI-assisted workflows, maintainer expertise, security tooling and funding to harden their code.

title: One Loop From Robot Demonstration to Deployed Policy
summary: Amazon and Hugging Face described a single pipeline for training robots: record a human demonstration straight into a cloud storage bucket, store it with byte-level deduplication so repeated frames are not saved twice, train by streaming the data from the Hub instead of downloading a copy, then deploy the resulting policy and feed its new recordings back into the same loop.

title: RustDesk Adds Unattended Remote Access on Wayland
summary: RustDesk, the open source alternative to TeamViewer, now supports true unattended remote access on Wayland — the display system that has been replacing the decades-old X11 on Linux desktops.

title: Anthropic Writes Up What Goes Wrong When AI Agents Work in Teams
summary: Anthropic published research on multi-agent systems — setups where several AI agents split a job between them instead of one assistant doing all of it.

title: GitHub Puts Agents Into the Steps Around the Code
summary: GitHub showed how four of its agent apps handle the work that surrounds writing software — scoping a feature, checking it for security problems, rolling it out, and shipping it — without leaving GitHub.

title: GitHub Logged Eight Service Incidents in July
summary: GitHub's monthly availability report counts eight incidents that degraded its services in July, after nine in May and six in June.

title: A Reality Check on AI in Drug Discovery
summary: Science published an assessment of where AI-assisted drug discovery actually stands and what still has to happen before it changes medicine.

title: Working With AI Feels More Like Leading a Team Than Doing the Work
summary: A developer argues that the skill AI tools now demand is the one managers already have: setting direction, checking work, and deciding what is good enough.

title: AI Helped Move a 250,000-Line Weather Model Onto GPUs
summary: Researchers published their account of using AI assistance to port a 250,000-line legacy weather simulation to run on GPUs — the chips that make modern AI training fast, and which also run scientific simulations far quicker than ordinary processors.

title: Fast Scientific Python Now Runs Inside the Browser
summary: Numba — a tool that speeds up Python by compiling the slow numerical parts down to machine code — now works in JupyterLite, a version of the Jupyter notebook that runs entirely in a browser tab with no server behind it.

title: Firefox on the iPhone Now Blocks Ads Out of the Box
summary: Previously covered on 2026-08-15: Firefox became the last major browser where the ad blocker uBlock Origin still works in full.

title: Anthropic Publishes the Instructions It Gives Claude
summary: Anthropic now lists Claude's system prompts — the standing instructions the assistant is given before you type anything — in its public release notes.

title: A Resale Market Has Grown Up Around AI Credits
summary: A report describes the brokers who buy and resell access to AI models — the credits companies pay for by the word.

title: A New Open Model Is Strong but Talks Itself in Circles
summary: Developer Simon Willison put Qwen 3.

title: Keyword Lists Were Used to Cancel Billions in Research Grants
summary: Higher Ed Dive obtained the federal keyword lists used to screen research grants, and traces how matching a word on a list led to billions of dollars in cancelled funding.

title: A Step-by-Step Timeline of an AI Lab Break-In
summary: Hugging Face published a technical reconstruction of the July 2026 intrusion at a frontier AI lab, laying out the incident as a timeline of how the attack unfolded around the lab's AI agents rather than as a summary after the fact.

title: Zero-Knowledge Proofs, Explained Briefly
summary: A short walkthrough of zero-knowledge proofs: a method for proving a statement is true without handing over the information behind it.

title: Anthropic Releases Claude Opus 5
summary: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5, the newest model in its high-end tier.

title: OpenAI Halves the Price of GPT-5.6 Sol
summary: OpenAI cut the price of its GPT-5.

title: An AI Bug-Fixing Tool Was Turned Into a Way In
summary: Security firm Wiz describes how GitHub Copilot's "Autofix" feature — which proposes code fixes automatically — could be manipulated to compromise Snowflake's internal Jira system.

title: A Fake Think Tank Built to Influence Chatbots
summary: Responsible Statecraft reports that Israel set up a think tank that appears to exist mainly so AI chatbots will cite it.

title: A Librarian's Guide to Turning AI Off
summary: Librarian Jessamyn West published a practical list of how to disable or avoid the AI features now switched on by default in search engines, browsers, phones, and office software.

title: Same Machines, 33 Points More Use — Only the Order Changed
summary: A team writing on Hugging Face's blog describes running the same cluster of AI chips 33 percentage points closer to full use without buying anything, purely by changing the order jobs run in.

title: DuckDB Previews Version 2.0
summary: DuckDB published a preview of the highlights coming in version 2.

title: Computer Memory Costs Five Times What It Did a Year Ago
summary: Tom's Hardware reports that memory prices have climbed roughly 500% in twelve months — up to ten times the cheapest levels ever tracked.

title: Apple Changes How Apps Work in the European Union
summary: Apple published a set of changes for apps distributed in the EU.

title: Cursor Launches a GitHub Alternative
summary: Cursor, the AI code editor, has launched Origin — its own service for storing and hosting code, the job GitHub does for most of the software industry.

title: Meta Releases an Open AI Model That Runs on Your Own Machine
summary: Meta published Muse Glimmer, an open source model that handles both text and images, can carry out multi-step tasks, and runs locally instead of in someone else's data centre.

title: A 25-Year-Old Video Patent Expires, Clearing a Problem for Linux
summary: A Brazilian patent covering video technology has run out, ending a long-standing legal complication for Linux.

title: Search That Compares Every Word, Not Just the Whole Document
summary: Sentence Transformers, one of the most widely used open source search libraries, now supports multi-vector — or "late interaction" — models.

title: How Much Memory an AI Agent Needs Depends on How Capable It Already Is
summary: IBM Research tested how much accumulated memory an AI agent actually needs, comparing three configurations across models of different strength.

title: Stripe Is Buying the Place Companies Go to Buy AI
summary: OpenRouter, the service that lets a business reach hundreds of different AI models through one account and one bill, announced it is joining Stripe, the company that processes online payments for a large share of the internet.

title: OpenAI Says It Will Slow Down Where Models Get Good at Hacking
summary: OpenAI published its thinking on how quickly to release models as they become more capable at cyber tasks — the same skills that help defenders find security holes also help attackers exploit them.

title: A Case for Giving AI a Whiteboard Instead of a Chat Window
summary: A GitHub engineer argues that chat is fine for saying what you want but terrible for tracking what an AI assistant actually did — the work disappears up the scroll.

title: Remote Workers Reported the Highest Well-Being in a Study of 7,700 People
summary: Researchers at the University of Colorado Boulder surveyed 7,700 employees and found that those working remotely reported better well-being than their on-site counterparts.

title: NVIDIA Releases a Voice Model You Can Run Yourself
summary: NVIDIA published Magpie TTS, a text-to-speech system with open weights, meaning anyone can download it and run it on their own hardware in several languages.

title: Squeezing AI Models Down to Four Bits Without Wrecking Them
summary: Previously covered on 2026-08-13: Liquid AI released LFM2.

title: Go 1.27 Is Out
summary: The Go team shipped version 1.

title: GitHub Explains the August 17 Outage and What It Is Changing
summary: GitHub published an account of the outage that degraded its services on August 17, along with the reliability work it is committing to next.

title: AI Companies Are Cutting Books Apart to Scan Them
summary: Anna's Archive argues that AI companies are buying physical books and destroying them in the process of digitising them, since slicing the spine off is the fastest way to feed pages through a scanner.

title: AliExpress Is Fingerprinting Visitors Through Their Audio Hardware
summary: A developer traced a strange bug in their Bluetooth headphones, which kept dropping the connection to a second device, back to AliExpress running silent audio fingerprinting in the background of its web pages.

title: A Malicious Software Package Ran Its Payload Before Anyone Pressed Run
summary: Security researchers at SafeDep found a package in Rust's public library index that executes hostile code while software is being built, not when it is later run.

title: A Small Model That Plays Piano With You
summary: A developer trained a 125-million-parameter model that autocompletes piano playing and runs entirely on the device rather than in a data centre.

title: Mojo Is Now Open Source
summary: Modular has opened the source code of Mojo, the programming language it built to write high-performance AI code with Python-like syntax.

title: Draft Models That Make Inference Up to 3.2x Faster
summary: Liquid AI released DSpark draft model checkpoints for three models in its LFM2.
